description: Exploratory demo cases, not a held-out accuracy benchmark. No clip depicts an identified real-world theft suspect.

shelf.title: Woman in a Store Placing Products Respectively
shelf.creator: Gustavo Fring / Pexels
shelf.use_note: Normal product handling. No criminal allegation or endorsement implied. Silent resized excerpt used in an explanatory demo; original asset is not relicensed as Apache-2.0.

basket.title: A Woman Carrying a Shopping Basket
basket.creator: Kampus Production / Pexels
basket.use_note: Normal shopping and visual occlusion. No criminal allegation or endorsement implied. Original asset is not relicensed as Apache-2.0.

film.title: The Kleptomaniac (1905)
film.creator: Edwin S. Porter / Edison Manufacturing Company
film.license: Public Domain Mark 1.0; expired film copyright as identified by Wikimedia Commons
film.use_note: Dramatised fictional theft, not actual CCTV evidence. Silent excerpts only. Historical low-resolution material is a domain-shift stress case, not representative modern camera accuracy.

cases.title: Normal product handling
cases.description: A person handles and places products. Counting and dwell are measurable; product handling alone does not establish theft.
cases.challenge: Object interaction, cropped body, ordinary retail activity.

cases.title: Shopping through occlusion
cases.description: A shopper and basket move behind foreground shelving. Missing visual evidence can interrupt a track and reset dwell.
cases.challenge: Moving foreground occlusion and a partly visible person.

cases.title: Staged bread-taking scene
cases.description: An excerpt from a 1905 drama shows a person approaching the bread display, taking an item and moving away. The supplied rules do not classify that sequence as theft.
cases.challenge: Small object, hand–object interaction, grayscale film and motion.

cases.title: Staged department-store scene
cases.description: A crowded shop scene from the same drama contains handling and concealment. A person detector can observe people while missing the meaning of the action.
cases.challenge: Crowding, occlusion, small objects and identity fragmentation.
